text:
maya.prod: uploaded a quick Figma prototype for the org settings panel — roles matrix + invite modal. can folks skim and flag obvious blockers? https://www.figma.com/file/XXX (only the top 2 frames matter)

alex.design: looked — nice direction. two main options: compact table (dense) vs cards (scannable). my vote: table for power users, cards for newcomers.

sam.eng: table is easier to implement for bulk operations (select row, change role). cards need more JS for inline editing.

maya.prod: good point. can we do a hybrid? table by default, toggle to cards for 'simple mode'?

jess.devex: hybrid feels heavy. maybe default table with a short onboarding tooltip that highlights invite flow and SSO settings. simpler code path.

alex.design: +1 to tooltip. also accessibility note: current contrast for the role pills is borderline (light green on white). need WCAG AA.

maya.prod: noted — @alex can you provide updated color tokens? tagging @taylor for security/SAML placement: where should the SSO toggle live? top-level org settings or inside a security tab?

taylor.sec: SSO toggle needs to be visible on the main org screen (customers expect it there), but advanced config links to Security -> SSO. so: toggle + 'configure' link. make sure toggle has a confirmation modal for disabling.

sam.eng: confirm modal should include text: "Disabling SSO will allow password logins for existing users". Also we should log that action to audit.

maya.prod: copy suggestions for invite modal — current: 'Invite team members' with button 'Send invites'. alternatives?

alex.design: try shorter, clearer: header: 'Invite members' body: 'Enter emails or paste a CSV. Assign role and optional project access.' primary button: 'Send invite' secondary: 'Copy invite link' (if link allowed).

jess.devex: UX question: do we allow invite links by default? security typically prefers email-only.

taylor.sec: no default. keep link generation behind a secondary dropdown with caution copy: 'Invite links bypass email verification; use only for trusted groups.' Also ensure link creation requires 2FA for org admins.

maya.prod: good constraints. need to show audit log entry for link generation and for role changes. how should we surface audit search? quick filter at top or separate page?

sam.eng: pref top-level quick filter with presets: "Invite events", "Role changes", "SSO changes" that jump into the audit stream. deeper filters on a separate audit page.

alex.design: UI pattern suggestion: chips for presets + free text search + date range. small affordance to export CSV.

jess.devex: accessibility nit: audit rows need keyboard focus and aria-live on new events if stream is live.

maya.prod: think about roles matrix semantics: currently we show permissions as checkmarks per role. suggestion to allow toggling at role level (edit role -> change permission set) vs user-level overrides. opinions?

taylor.sec: role-level changes are safer. avoid per-user permission toggles unless explicitly enabled. if we add per-user overrides, show strong warnings and require audit logging.

sam.eng: implement role templates first. per-user overrides can be a future opt-in flag in org settings.

alex.design: tiny copy tweak for roles page header: change "Roles & permissions" -> "Roles & permissions (organization-wide)" to reduce confusion about project-level roles.

maya.prod: agree. also add breadcrumb: Org > Roles.

eng-bot: deploy-preview created for branch feature/rbac-ui-compact. Preview: https://deploy.preview/redwood/PR-456

sam.eng: thanks bot. i'll check perf on the table renders for 2k users. if row virtualization needed, i'll follow up.

maya.prod: wrapping up decisions: default to table, onboarding tooltip, SSO toggle on main page with configure link+confirm modal, invite links behind dropdown with warning + 2FA requirement, audit presets at top, role templates only, per-user overrides opt-in. any objections?

alex.design: no objections. i'll push color fixes and updated mock with accessible contrast tomorrow.

taylor.sec: no objections from security. I'll add the 2FA requirement to the spec.

jess.devex: will draft developer-facing doc and small code snippets for the SDK to show invite API examples (email vs link).

sam.eng: will prototype virtualization if perf issues.

maya.prod: great — thanks everyone. i'll update the PR description and include a short checklist for launch:
- color tokens WCAG AA
- confirm modal copy
- audit log presets
- invite link warning + 2FA gating
- onboarding tooltip copy

maya.prod: ping me here if anything else comes up. :thumbsup:
